The 3x3 is a real overlay on the body now, not a popover: 9 buttons at x{8,174,340} y{36,190,344}, each aligned inside its own grid cell by the code it carries, `cc` marked on. Three minions back. SCRUB ZOOM: ext/demo/stage.js:180 `magnifier(set,zoomed,whole)`, private, uses the `zoom` PROPERTY not transform:scale — 'scale looks identical and lies, because a scaled box still occupies its unscaled size, so nothing re-lays-out'. MASTER/DUPLICATES: a literal shared Item is ruled out — `parent` is a single scalar (List.js:17) and `views` is one-entry-per-Item (workspace.js:207), so one Item cannot have two mounts. assign.now: Waves 1-3 live and verified; 4-6 designed in doc/plan.md

log.msg: Edge split verified end to end: click the right edge and a ghost takes the right half (187 of 373px), move past the midline and it flips to `before`, Escape cancels with the tree untouched (41 panels), a left click commits (41 -> 43). ⚠ The geometry needed a real fix first — hit-testing showed the GRIP won three of four edges (its target straddles a seam by 0.625rem) and the bar's own centred quick-split button won the fourth, so the strips reached nothing. Resolved SPATIALLY rather than by z-order: outer 0.7rem stays the grip's, the split band starts after it, the top band starts below the bar. That is Mike's own 'what if the child's edge is the same as the parent's edge' question, answered.

Selection lands in the rail: clicking a panel body opens ext/drawer with template/tone/align/mode, 43 controls, no errors — the thing the drawer was extracted for. properties.js is imported LAZILY from tools.js on the focus event, because a static import would close the ring workspace -> tools -> properties -> workspace, which breaks on deep reloads only. Also dropped panel.css's `:has(.panel-props)` guard on the focus ring: it existed so a workspace with no inspector never marked a selection nothing acted on, and the rail is now always that reader.
Regression sweep: 11 pages clean (ext/Panel, ext/drawer, ext/layout, ext/editor, ext/LayoutTool, web/layout/flex, web/layout/grid, styles/layouts, styles/sections, ui, framework).

assign.now: Display word + live duplicates landed; three build minions out on insert/display-overlay/text

log.msg: `display` is a panel word now: block|flex|grid, an icon opening a pick on the bar and a row in the inspector, written to .panel-body as panel-d-*. Verified panel-d-block -> panel-d-flex through the bar.

MASTER + LIVE DUPLICATES land, and they work: duplicated a changelog panel, changed the MASTER's template to clock, and BOTH bodies became panel-t-clock (clock_count 2). Architecture is the id-reference the research pointed at — `data.mirror` holds the master's id, `Panel.get/set` delegate for Panel.shared = template/tone/align/display/seed while grow/mode/dir stay local (a copy in a narrow column is still that column's width). Three guards, each one a real failure mode: `?? this` in get() so a CLOSED master leaves an ordinary panel rather than breaking every copy; mirror() collapses a mirror-of-a-mirror to the original at CREATION so the get() cycle cannot be built; and repaint never calls set, so the change listener cannot echo. ⚠ `change` carries key/value/old and NOT the item (Item.emit), so the root listener repaints every mirror on any change rather than growing an event signature four other listeners read.

Alt-drop is the gesture: PanelDrag.release() reads e.altKey at DROP, not at grab — a copy is a decision you make once you can see where it lands, and Draggable needs no new state. Only the EDGE path copies; a plain reorder within one list is never a duplicate. A `content_copy` button on the bar is the same verb for a panel you would rather not drag.

Alt-drop verified: grabbed the first leaf by its handle, dropped it in the outer fifth of the last leaf with Alt held — the original stayed put at x=23 and a copy landed (4 leaves -> 5). Same mirror() call the bar button uses, whose linkage was already proved by the two-clocks test.

Persistence round-trip proved, which was the real risk in the id-reference design: created a live duplicate, let the saver drain, RELOADED the page, and the copy came back still LIVE — changing the master's template to haze turned both bodies into panel-t-haze. `data.mirror` is a plain string so it survives toJSON/hydrate untouched, and hydrate only re-mints an id when it sees a DUPLICATE, which a reference never causes. Mike's /data/panels.json backed up before the test and restored after (it is gitignored, so there is nothing to check out).

Text layers built: ext/Panel/text.js + text.css (the two files this minion owned). text_layers($body) is ONE delegated listener over p/h1-h6/li/blockquote/span.h1-4 — mouseover outlines (.panel-text-hot, dashed), click selects (.panel-text-on, solid --prim) and e.stopPropagation()s so workspace.js's own panel-selection click never also fires. Announces `panel-text` on document, detail a View wrapping the element (or null on deselect/toggle-off) — text_fields($el) reads it. text_fields($el) draws level (h1/h2/h3/h4/body — writes ONLY the matching class, never a font-size), weight and tracking (direct inline font-weight/letter-spacing, `normal` = empty string so it clears rather than fights the levels own weight), and align (text-align) as panel-btn rows reusing glyph() from glyphs.js. node --check clean. NOT wired: workspace.js view() needs `text_layers($body);` beside `align_grid(item, $body);`, plus the import — left for Mike per the brief.

assign.now: All three minion modules integrated and verified

log.msg: Three build minions landed and are integrated. INSERT: a + that rides a split's gaps, verified tracking across the workspace (0 -> 517 -> 402 -> 918 -> 1454px) and inserting on click. TEXT: hover mark, selection, and 15 controls in the rail (5 levels + 3 weights + 3 tracking + 4 align) — and panel_focused stayed FALSE, so stopPropagation correctly keeps a text click from also selecting the panel. DISPLAY: grid draws a track line with the browser's own resolved px (100px), flex draws the axis with each child's flex-grow.

Three defects found reviewing minion code, all fixed before wiring. (1) insert.js used `coalesce()`, which is a DRAG throttle that unbinds on the first pointerup — one click anywhere in the split retired the bar's tracking permanently; replaced with its own persistent rAF throttle. The minion had spotted and documented this itself but shipped it. (2) insert.css revealed on `.panel:hover:not(:has(.panel:hover))`, which can NEVER match a split — a split contains panels by definition — so the bar would never have appeared; the right question is whether this is the deepest split, so the test is `.panel-items:hover:not(:has(.panel-items:hover))`. (3) At z-index 5 over the gaps, the insert bar would have stolen every drag-to-resize on the workspace; it now stands down while a grip is hovered, so a seam is the grip's and anywhere else is the +.

⚠ `live_axes(mode, dir)` is built and its truth table is right (grid both axes, flex row = cross only, flex col = the other, block neither) but is deliberately NOT wired to the 3x3. The existing grid controls a leaf's own CONTENT alignment, which is live in every display mode; live_axes describes SELF-alignment against a parent, a control that does not exist yet. Wiring it to the 3x3 would grey out buttons that work. It waits for the control it actually describes.

log.msg: Mike's insert-bar complaints, both real, both fixed. It was full-height so it covered the grip for the seam's ENTIRE length — the resize handle could never appear — and it had no visible boundary. It is now a 2.2rem STUB at the head of the seam with a surface, a border and a shadow, so the grip keeps the rest. It also no longer offers the two OUTER gaps: those are the panel's own edges, where clicking already opens the split preview, so the + was hiding a better gesture behind a worse one. Verified the grip is hit-testable again at both the middle and near the top of a seam.

T enters text entry on any panel — verified on 3 of 3 leaves: contenteditable=plaintext-only, focused, the whole run pre-selected so the first keystroke replaces it, typing lands, Escape ends. ⚠ A panel with no prose (a scene, a clock) GROWS a line rather than doing nothing — 'on any panel' means the shortcut cannot be right only where a template happened to ship a paragraph. Enter deliberately does NOT end editing: a heading may legitimately wrap.

Two structural answers to Mike's 'we don't have a container panel? how do we drag something inside?'. `Panel.split(dir)` is `divide()`'s else-branch, named: ALWAYS become a container whatever the parent runs. The two were one verb only for as long as nothing could ask for the inside. PanelDrag now reads the MIDDLE of a leaf as a nest target — edge means beside (divide), middle means inside (split) — with an inset frame preview so the two drops never read alike. Tested after edge() and before locate(), the same ordering the edge zones already needed. Also: wrap() puts a selected text layer in a div/section/figure that takes its place in the flow and adopts it, verified DIV holding P.

In-place text overlay: a fixed badge on the selected run reading `h2 · 58ch × 3` — what it IS and how long its line runs, the two facts you cannot get by looking, since a heading and a bold paragraph are the same picture. A `ch` is MEASURED off a canvas in the element's own font, never derived from font-size, which is wrong by a third on any condensed face. ⚠ The 45-75ch rule is applied ONLY once the text wraps: judged on every run it flags every label on the page — SHIPPED is 11ch and there is nothing wrong with it — and a warning that fires on correct work is one you learn to ignore. Verified updating per element (h4 · 49ch vs h4 · 8ch × 2 NARROW).

⚠ FINDING for Mike, from testing rather than reading: selecting anything opens the properties rail, and the rail PUSHES (.app yields 19rem), so the whole workspace reflows under the pointer. Measured — successive clicks at freshly-measured coordinates still landed on the PREVIOUS element, because the 0.18s push moves the target between pointerdown and pointerup. It follows directly from the drawer's founding decision (a properties panel must never cover what you are editing), so it is his call, not a bug to quietly fix. Options if it bites: overlay the rail on a full-window workspace only, hold the push until the pointer leaves, or reserve the strip permanently once anything has been selected.
